sentences.text:
The petitioners and respondent No.2 herein most respectfully submit this Joint Compromise Application seeking compounding of the offences enumerated in the criminal complaint filed by Respondent No.1 Police in Crime No.142/2021 for offences punishable under Sections 498A, 34 of IPC and Sections 3 & 4 of DP Act,
currently pending before the I Addl. Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bengaluru as below:-
NC: 2025:KHC:25304 HC-KAR 1.

entities.text: I Addl. Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The 1st Accused/ son of the Petitioners had instituted Matrimonial Case No.3099/2021 before the Hon'ble Principal Judge, Family Court, Bengaluru, seeking a decree of divorce.
During the course of mediation, parties had amicably settled their disputes and agreed for divorce with the accused No.1.
Consequently, a decree of divorce was passed, wherein she expressly consented to compound the aforementioned criminal case.
2. The Respondent No.2 is not inclined to pursue the criminal proceedings in Crime No.142/2021, as the dispute has already been amicably settled.
The matter is under investigation.
Respondent No.2 has formally withdrawn all allegations made in the complaint.
Consequently, the complaint filed against the Petitioner have become infructuous and are liable to be compounded in the interest of justice.

3. The Petitioner humbly submits that the offences mentioned herein are compoundable with the leave of this Hon'ble Court, in terms of the law NC:
2025:KHC:25304 HC-KAR laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in (2012) 10 SCC 303 (Gian Singh's case).
4. The Petitioner humbly requests that this Hon'ble Court pleased to be read the averments made in the main petition as part & parcel of this application to avoid repetitive averments.

WHEREFORE, the Petitioners and the Respondent No.2 most humbly pray this Hon'ble Court to pleased to accept the joint compromise application and permit the Respondent No.2 to compound the offences against the petitioners in Crime No.142/2021 for offences punishable under Sections 498A, 34 of IPC and Sections 3 & 4 of DP Act, currently pending before the I Addl. Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bengaluru, in the ends of justice.
5. Respondent No.2/complainant admits the compromise and submits that she has no objection to allow the petition.

entities.text: I Addl. Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The terms and conditions of compromise NC: 2025:KHC:25304 HC-KAR petition is legal and equitable.

The same is accepted and accordingly, following:
ORDER (i) The petition filed under Section 482 of Cr.P.C, is allowed.
